subject.title: feat: add a safe API for writing skills

question: Should OpenClaw establish `skills.write.*` as a new permanent public Gateway contract, or keep the write service internal and preserve the existing proposal/install RPC namespaces?
rationale: The branch creates a cross-platform public API and claims plugin use, while current plugin guidance separates in-process Plugin SDK contracts from external Gateway RPCs; implementation review cannot choose that permanent owner boundary safely.

options.title: Keep one existing contract
options.body: Keep `skillsWriteService` internal, route existing proposal and install methods through it, and consider only non-duplicative RPCs separately.

options.title: Adopt the new namespace
options.body: Approve `skills.write.*` as the replacement contract and include an explicit compatibility and deprecation plan for the existing proposal methods.

options.title: Pause the public API
options.body: Retain only the bounded snapshot-refresh or internal consolidation work until a sponsored plugin or external-client requirement defines the necessary surface.

recommendation.title: Keep one existing contract
recommendation.body: Keep `skillsWriteService` internal, route existing proposal and install methods through it, and consider only non-duplicative RPCs separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner most directly to skill write safety and install-policy boundaries that determine whether direct mutation should become a public contract.
